ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$, with $\angle C=46^\circ$. Connecting $OA$, what is the measure of $\angle OAB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure:\\
Connect OB,\\
$\because \angle C=46^\circ$,\\
$\therefore \angle AOB=92^\circ$,\\
Also, $\because OA=OB$,\\
$\therefore \angle OAB=\angle OBA=(180-92^\circ)÷2=\boxed{44^\circ}$.

The line segment OA has been drawn in the figure, AB is a chord of the circle, the angle at point C is ∠ACB, and the problem gives ∠C = 46°. Reasoning: Connect OB. Because ∠ACB is the inscribed angle subtending arc AB, the central angle ∠AOB subtending the same arc AB is equal to 2 times the inscribed angle, that is, ∠AOB = 2 × 46° = 92°. method.method_draft: From the image, read that AB is a chord of the circle, C is another point on the circle, and OA is the radius to endpoint A of chord AB. From the text, use ∠ACB = 46°. Draw the tangent line to the circle at A. By the tangent-chord theorem, the angle between this tangent and chord AB equals the inscribed angle ∠ACB, so it is 46°. Since the radius OA is perpendicular to the tangent at A, ∠OAB is complementary to 46°, giving ∠OAB = 90° − 46° = 44°.
